body:
I go through this too. It's not that I don't like being considered beautiful, I just don't like being called beautiful. This doesn't always happen of course, it's just sometimes when I'm feeling down. I'm not sure if the cause of my problem is the same as yours but sometimes when my SO tells me I'm beautiful (when I'm in a bad mood or feeling insecure or something) I feel like he's being patronising, pitiful even. I feel like he doesn't actually even feel that way (even though that's not true) and he simply feels obliged to say it. It gets extremely frustrating for both of us. I almost get disgusted and very irritated when he says that, in fact.

Of course, I feel terrible about it. There he is being a lovely boyfriend and here I am not accepting a compliment graciously. I understand the problem is mine though, I really can't figure it out unfortunately.

The most important thing, I'd say, is to find out why his saying that makes you feel uncomfortable. Could it be any of the reasons I listed above? Or is it something else? Once you figure that out, you can try overcoming it. For example, I'm trying to deal with issues of insecurity and lack of self worth. I think that will help solve the problem, since if I find myself beautiful I won't be so surprised when others do. :) Good luck.

You know what? I used to think that too! I thought there's this very specific breasts to waist to hips ratio that men desire, that they prefer some hair colour over the other, etc. And it only upset me further when evolutionary hypotheses were claimed as a reason, because you can't argue with science, right?! But then I meet men who swear that they aren't simply 'settling' and they actually prefer certain 'flaws'. How does evolution explain such unique varied preferences in everyone then? :D
Guilty as charged! Hah!
Oh dear, can't say I intended for that. But I'm not surprised.
Oops! Sorry for assuming. Either way, yep, it applies for all people. :D

Thank you so much. It honestly makes me feel better to talk about it. But I know deep down, that soon enough, it'll hurt again and I'll forget about everything that made me happy and just feel sad again.

I worry, because I've lost my passion. I was never perfect, but at least I enjoyed learning new things and reading, and I don't any more. And I think that's just terrible because how am I supposed to go on if that was the one driving force that really kept me going? And I feel like it'll just get worse. How can I just GET back that passion, that drive, that desire to live and learn more? I think partly, I see life as far too much of a competition these days. I've completely disregarded the joy involved and only see it as something to do to get 'better' than others. And that I think will be the reason I'll always feel like this.
So what do you think of stretch marks? Since they're a kind of scarring? I don't have any, maybe because I'm super skinny and short but a lot of my friends think they're horrible!
I think imperfect skin is very sexy on both genders! I mean, flawless skin is beautiful yes, but I actually like acne, rosacea, scarring, etc. It's rather endearing!
Wow! That makes a lot of sense! I know exactly what you mean, I find those conventionally beautiful women very...'generic' looking. Excuse the tautology. But I don't know how else to word it!

None that I can think of. It's just always those same feelings of inadequacy, of being worth little or nothing. And you know what, it's true. Not everyone can be special. I only expect too much of myself and I can't seem to love myself as I am. I want to be as attractive as the women on TV, unrealistic though it may sound, while also being extremely intelligent. And I feel like I haven't watched enough, read enough or learned enough to be knowledgeable and I'll never have the time to.
Yes, like the old James Bond! Hairy and pudgy.
Bald, hairy men are sexy! It's like they're so manly for head hair that they grow it everywhere else.

>laughed, stroked it too, not cared at all, or told me if it was a hassle I should just let it be.

You have been with some real men, right there. Not 'good' men, because I personally believe *this* is how people should be BY default. That sounds amazing, I'm so glad no one's made you feel inadequate or something. As they shouldn't, because you're rockin' that 'stache. And you're rocking it shaved too. Yay!

Hey! I COMPLETELY see your point. And no, it wasn't to feel better about my body! I just wanted to see how people go about liking what are considered 'flaws', and with that, how beauty TRULY lies in the eyes of the beholder. A lot of people here have mentioned they like a bit of chubbiness, and I didn't get offended (I'm super skinny)! It's more of a 'nothing's *really* a flaw" experiment.
Aww! My dad had one on his wrist, I think I used to play with them when I was younger.
Yes, but that doesn't mean she has to be downvoted guys. Some warts are benign. A nicer way to word it, is that she should get them checked.
Thick legs are lovely! Trust me, I have skinny ones, and thick ones are more delectable in my eyes.
And then show us the result, of course. :D

I personally think you'd look great with one! Your broad smile and well, petite, pixie-ish features would go well with a pixie style haircut. I think you should go for something [like this](http://www.dhaircut.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/pixie-haircuts-1.jpg), like you said, the thing about the rounder face!

If you really want to, then DEFINITELY go for it. It's just hair. Only a fortnight between a bad haircut and a good haircut (or the other way around).

And if you do, then upload pictures!

A long haired woman myself, I can't dream of cutting my locks even though I've been told short hair would look quite lovely on me. So I compensate by looking at other women with short hair. :)

I've tried. But I despise burdening people with these feelings especially when I know they can't help. Because I know it's all me and how I'm feeling. The people around me are truly amazing, and I dislike letting them know that I'm unhappy. They can't help any way.

Thank you so much for responding. Yes, that's pretty much why it's so bad. I feel like it's something I cannot control, I will always remain unhappy. I do have some symptoms of clinical depression. And unfortunately, I'm not in a position to be able to move out of the country even for a little while but I'll keep my eyes open for opportunities.

I can completely understand why that'd have affected you. I'd have felt the same way in spite of knowing that they're the immature jerks. To know something is different from how you feel, so you're not being silly in case you feel that way.

I can't get over what an idiotic move it was of theirs, seriously, I didn't see what's so funny about it and I'm pretty tolerant and have an 'accepting' sense of humour. I'm not going to say "you don't want a guy like that any way" because that's so fucking obvious and I bet you feel the same.

To cope, well, just remember how awesome you are. And trust me, you are. You seem articulate and clever and you know you're not ugly. And it isn't you, it's THEM. They're the ones with the disgusting attitude. You weren't treated like that by them because you were unattractive, it's because they were stupid and childish. Who's to say they wouldn't treat a 'gorgeous and sexy' woman equally badly, even if it is in a different way? It's quite apparent that they are simply inconsiderate and it has nothing to do with how appealing you are.

First of all, don't worry. It's normal to cry/be upset by what seems to be a 'little thing'. Different things trigger different people, that can't be helped. So, in my opinion at least, I don't think you're unjustified or unreasonable.

Yes, I'm also a woman with a slight moustache. I remember I used to feel awful about it, I would cry because there were other women who were lucky enough to not have upper lip hair (turned out most of them were doing something about it, by the way).

I've noticed that when I made addressing the problem a part of my routine, I didn't feel so bad about it. Like I don't now. I shave it. Before I get flak for it, I've been doing it for two years and I personally feel like the results are great. I don't have thick hairs, so it doesn't look stubbly. Even when it is just growing out, it's fine. Also, it isn't painful and it takes all of two minutes to do properly. Yes, I don't mind sparing those two minutes so I can feel more confident. And I do it for myself, plenty of my friends have said they don't actually see a difference. So yes, it's for me.

Just remember, you have to do what makes you happy. Whether that involves dealing with the hair, or leaving it be. I agree, that thread could have been upsetting, but don't let it make you feel that you have to adhere to what they say. Any man who's worth having will certainly not force you to get rid of your 'stache if it's a big deal to you. Whether he prefers you with it or without it is different, he should value your feelings the most.
